name: Crack a fetch on turn 1-2 for a land that unlocks a hand card
intent: On turn 1 or 2, once open-land-unlocks has had first refusal, play a fetch from hand (Misty Rainforest, Scalding Tarn) and crack it for whatever library land would unlock some other hand card - a library Island (or an Island-subtype dual) unlocking Curator of Mysteries' Cycling {U}. Both fetches reach Island equally, so which one gets cracked decides which fetch's OTHER reach survives for later: Misty Rainforest is this deck's only route to Forest (this deck's most important colour, per fetch-untapped-shock's own colour order Forest, Island, Mountain) and Scalding Tarn its only route to Mountain (the least important); the prefer tier searches_for_any:[Mountain] matches Scalding Tarn alone (Misty Rainforest's own template never names Mountain), spending the less valuable reach and reserving Misty Rainforest for a future Forest need. The activate move's own source carries a prefer:[{unlocks_by_basic_search:true}] tier of its own, so a second untapped fetch left over from an earlier turn's open-land-idle is never the one cracked in place of the fetch this turn's own land drop just played, and a source whose only reach is a non-basic is never preferred over one that reaches a free basic. Its own choose_cards pick prefers a basic first, then a shockland, paying life only when the fetch's own find needs it. This play's own true key now reads unlocks_by_basic_search rather than the broader unlocks_by_search: a fetch whose only reach is a non-basic shockland no longer fires this play at all (it would pay the fetch's own life cost on top of the found shock's), matching open-shock-unlocks' own narrowed false key. That leaves one gap: a hand with no direct shock AND a fetch reaching only a non-basic - neither P nor F applies; open-land-idle does still apply though, since its own I tier 3 (FETCH) has no `unlocks`/`unlocks_by_search` gate at all - the fetch still gets played, just not cracked productively the same turn, so the land drop itself is never lost, only the crack; documented as a known limit in docs/DECK-PIPELINE.md rather than worked around (living-end sits at the 12-play cap, with no room for a dedicated fetch-for-a-shock play). Stands down once open-land-unlocks would already fire, at 7 life or less, once the library is down to 5 cards or fewer, and whenever a tapped-entering land is also in hand (U's own new false key). Only turns 1-2, land drop available, mine, precombat main, empty stack.
